title: Lead generation tracking for BDRs on Mac: how to save hours every week
metaTitle: Lead generation tracking for BDRs on Mac: work faster with voice
description: Learn how to improve your lead generation tracking on Mac. Use voice to handle CRM entries, email drafting, and research without constant context switching.
intro: Lead generation tracking on Mac requires constant focus on your CRM, email, and research tabs. You can stop the manual grind by using your voice to manage these tasks instead of clicking through menus.
tldr: BDRs spend 60 percent of their week on admin tasks.
Manual data entry and email triage kill your sales velocity.
Lazur lets you dictate, research, and navigate your Mac using voice.
Stop wasting time on repetitive clicking and start selling more.

blocks.text: Why lead generation tracking feels slow

Your day as a BDR is filled with small, repetitive actions. You open a prospect record in Salesforce. You switch to LinkedIn to verify their role. You move to Gmail to draft an intro. You return to your CRM to log the activity. This constant movement between windows is where you lose your momentum.

Most BDRs report that note-taking and data input are their biggest time sinks. When you use a mouse to navigate every field, you slow yourself down. You also increase the chance of errors. Your lead generation tracking should be a background process, not a primary job duty.
Using voice to manage your sales stack

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It does not click buttons for you, but it acts as a bridge between your intent and your screen. When you hold ⌥ ⌘, you can ask about any element on your screen. If you cannot find the log button in your CRM, ask Lazur to point it out. It draws a circle around the target area.

Email is the core of your outreach. You likely handle over 100 messages a day. Instead of typing every response, use the dictation feature. Hold fn and speak your thoughts. Lazur turns your voice into clean, formatted text at your cursor. This works in Gmail, Slack, or any other app on your Mac.

Researching a company takes time. You browse their site, check their recent news, and look for their latest funding rounds. Lazur runs these jobs in the background. It uses its own Chrome tabs to gather information. You get a summary report back without leaving your current workspace.
Common mistakes in lead generation tracking

items: Waiting until the end of the day to log all your calls.
Keeping too many tabs open and losing your place.
Copying and pasting data between apps manually.
Ignoring the keyboard shortcuts for your main CRM.
Trying to remember prospect details instead of keeping records.

blocks.text: Keep your CRM, your email, and your research tools accessible. Use tools like SupaSidebar to group these tabs. When everything is in one place, you spend less time searching for windows. Use ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur where a specific tab is if you get lost in the clutter.

You handle sensitive prospect information. Lazur is designed for privacy. It only listens or looks at your screen when you hold the shortcut. Your audio and screenshots are sent to the AI to generate an answer and are not stored. Your content is never used to train models.

faq.question: Can Lazur fill out my CRM forms for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or interact with forms directly. It can guide you on where to click or dictate text into a field for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur is currently only available for macOS on Apple silicon and Intel chips. A Windows version is planned but not available today.

faq.question: Is my data safe with Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only processes your screen and audio when you actively hold the shortcut key. Data is not stored, and it is never used to train AI models.
